title: AI, ML & Image Processing – Subject Test

questions.q: Each node of a Bayesian network stores
options: the adjacency matrix of the entire graph
a conditional probability table given its parent nodes
a production rule with a certainty factor
questions.exp: A root node holds its prior; every other node holds P(node | parents).

questions.q: If the sentence 'AI is fun' is tokenized using whitespace as the delimiter, how many tokens are obtained?
questions.exp: The tokens are 'AI', 'is' and 'fun'.

questions.q: A classifier has precision 0.6 and recall 0.3. Its F1 score is

A disease has prevalence 1%. A test detects it with probability 0.9 (sensitivity) and gives a false positive with probability 0.1. A person tests positive. The probability of actually having the disease is about
A model that is too simple and has high bias typically suffers from
questions.exp: High bias means the model cannot capture the data pattern, giving poor training and test performance.

questions.q: Fuzzy set theory was introduced by
questions.exp: Lotfi A. Zadeh introduced fuzzy sets in 1965.

questions.q: In animation, automatic generation of the intermediate frames between two keyframes is called
questions.exp: Tweening (in-betweening) lets software fill in the frames between keyframes.

questions.q:
Statement I: The ReLU function is defined as f(x) = max(0, x).
Statement II: The output of ReLU is always bounded between 0 and 1.
Which option is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: ReLU returns x for positive x, so its output is unbounded above; Statement II is false.

questions.q: The degree of membership of an element in a fuzzy set always lies in the range
questions.exp: A fuzzy membership function maps elements to real values between 0 and 1 inclusive; {0,1} is the crisp case.

questions.q: The uncompressed size of 10 seconds of audio sampled at 8 kHz with 8 bits per sample and one channel is
questions.exp: 8000 samples/s × 1 byte × 1 channel × 10 s = 80,000 bytes.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A* search with an admissible heuristic finds an optimal path.
Reason (R): An admissible heuristic never overestimates the true cost to the goal.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Because h never overestimates, A* cannot skip a cheaper path, so optimality follows directly from admissibility.

questions.q: Which of the following is a commonly used technique for dimensionality reduction?
questions.exp: PCA projects data onto a few orthogonal directions of maximum variance.

questions.q: Which data structure is used by the Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm to keep track of the nodes to be explored?
questions.exp: BFS explores nodes level by level, so it needs a FIFO queue.

questions.q: In a k-nearest neighbour classifier with k = 3, the three nearest neighbours of a query point are labelled Red, Blue and Red. The predicted class is
questions.exp: Majority vote among the 3 neighbours gives Red (2 votes to 1).

questions.q: In the A* search algorithm, the evaluation function for a node n is
questions.exp: A* uses f(n) = g(n) + h(n), the cost so far plus the estimated cost to the goal.

questions.q: Which of the following problems is an example of regression?
options: Classifying an email as spam or not spam
Predicting the selling price of a house from its area and location
questions.exp: Regression predicts a continuous numeric value such as price.

questions.q: Which activation function is normally used in the output layer of a neural network for multi-class classification so that the outputs form a probability distribution?
questions.exp: Softmax exponentiates and normalises the outputs so they are positive and sum to 1.

questions.q: In steepest-ascent hill climbing, the next state is chosen as
options: the first neighbour better than the current state
a random neighbour even if it is worse
the best state among all neighbours of the current state
the state with the lowest path cost from the start
questions.exp: Steepest ascent examines all successors and moves to the best; it stops when none is better (local maximum).

questions.q: Which is the first fundamental step in digital image processing?
questions.exp: The process begins with acquiring the image; enhancement, restoration, compression and segmentation follow.

questions.q: Overlaying computer-generated objects on the user's view of the real world, as in the game Pokemon Go, is known as
questions.exp: AR adds digital content to the real environment; VR replaces the environment entirely.

questions.q: In expert system development, the person who interviews domain experts and encodes their knowledge into the knowledge base is called the
questions.exp: The knowledge engineer acquires, structures and represents expert knowledge.

questions.q: Which multimedia hardware component converts the analog signal from a microphone into digital samples?
questions.exp: A sound card contains an analog-to-digital converter for audio input and a DAC for output.

questions.q: Which of the following is a lossless image compression format?
questions.exp: PNG uses lossless DEFLATE compression; JPEG, MP3 and MPEG are lossy.

questions.q: In MYCIN, the certainty factor attached to a conclusion ranges from
questions.exp: MYCIN certainty factors lie between −1 and +1, allowing uncertain evidence to be combined.

questions.q: In Bresenham's line algorithm, the initial decision parameter is p0 = 2Δy − Δx. For a line from (0, 0) to (10, 4), what is p0?
In a Bayesian network with the chain A → B → C (A has no parent), the joint probability P(A, B, C) equals
questions.exp: The joint distribution is the product of each node's probability given its parents: P(A) P(B|A) P(C|B).

questions.q: Which of the following is primarily an audio-editing software?
questions.exp: Audacity edits and records audio; Blender and Maya are 3D/animation tools, Illustrator is vector graphics.

questions.q: For a cancer screening test, where missing a real patient is very costly, which metric should be maximised?
questions.exp: Recall = TP/(TP+FN); a high recall means few real cases are missed.

questions.q: Means-ends analysis, used by the General Problem Solver, works by
options: expanding nodes strictly level by level
repeatedly reducing the difference between the current state and the goal state
choosing a random action each time
pruning branches using alpha and beta values
questions.exp: GPS picks an operator that reduces the detected difference, setting its preconditions as sub-goals.

questions.q: A MIDI file mainly contains
options: sampled PCM waveform data of the sound
event instructions such as note on/off, pitch and instrument
questions.exp: MIDI stores performance events, not recorded sound, so files are tiny and playback depends on the synthesiser.

questions.q: The output of a sigmoid activation function for an input of 0 is
Which of the following search strategies is NOT guaranteed to find a solution in a search tree of infinite depth?
options: Uniform-cost search with positive step costs
questions.exp: DFS may go down an infinite branch forever and never reach the goal, so it is not complete.

questions.q: Text in which words or phrases are linked to other documents so that readers can navigate non-linearly is called
questions.exp: Hypertext links nodes of text; combined with other media it becomes hypermedia.

questions.q: In a fuzzy inference system, defuzzification is the process of
options: converting crisp inputs into fuzzy sets
adding noise to the membership function
converting the fuzzy output set into a single crisp value
questions.exp: Defuzzification (e.g. centroid method) produces a crisp output from the aggregated fuzzy set.

questions.q: The expert system MYCIN was developed for
options: diagnosing bacterial infections and recommending antibiotics
identifying chemical structures from mass spectra
questions.exp: MYCIN, a rule-based system from Stanford, diagnosed blood infections and suggested antibiotic therapy.

questions.q: Facts: P, Q. Rules: R1: P AND Q → R; R2: R → S; R3: S AND T → U. Forward chaining finally derives which set of facts?
questions.exp: R1 gives R, R2 gives S; R3 needs T which is unknown, so U is never derived.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an uninformed (blind) search strategy?
questions.exp: Greedy best-first search uses a heuristic h(n), so it is informed.

questions.q: A single-layer perceptron cannot learn which of the following Boolean functions?
questions.exp: XOR is not linearly separable, so one linear threshold unit cannot represent it.

questions.q: In an expert system, which component is responsible for telling the user how or why a conclusion was reached?
questions.exp: The explanation facility justifies the reasoning steps and conclusions to the user.

questions.q: In a production (rule-based) system, choosing one rule from the set of all rules whose conditions are currently satisfied is called
questions.exp: The matched rules form the conflict set; conflict resolution (priority, specificity, recency) selects the rule to fire.

questions.q: MP3 achieves its high compression mainly by
options: discarding sounds the human ear cannot perceive (psychoacoustic masking)
run-length encoding of the raw waveform only
questions.exp: MP3 (MPEG-1 Layer 3) is lossy perceptual coding followed by Huffman coding.

questions.q: For two fuzzy sets, an element has membership 0.3 in A and 0.7 in B. Using the standard fuzzy operators, its membership in A ∩ B is
questions.exp: Standard fuzzy intersection takes the minimum: min(0.3, 0.7) = 0.3.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector graphics file format?
questions.exp: SVG stores shapes and paths mathematically; JPEG, BMP and GIF are raster formats.

questions.q: The analog television standard used in India, running at 25 frames per second, is
questions.exp: India uses PAL (625 lines, 25 fps); NTSC (about 30 fps) is used in the USA and Japan.

questions.q: The Turing test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, is designed to check whether a machine can
options: solve any mathematical problem in polynomial time
store more data than a human brain
process images faster than a human
exhibit conversational behaviour indistinguishable from that of a human
questions.exp: In the imitation game a human judge cannot reliably tell the machine from a human through conversation.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical goal-driven (backward-chaining) application?
options: Firing alarms as sensor data keeps arriving
Adding every derivable fact from an order, as in XCON configuration
Generating all consequences of a new fact in a monitoring system
Diagnosing a suspected disease as in MYCIN or answering a Prolog query
questions.exp: Backward chaining starts from a hypothesis/goal and looks for rules and facts supporting it (MYCIN, Prolog).

questions.q: Macromedia/Adobe Authorware, an authoring tool, is based on which authoring metaphor?
questions.exp: Authorware builds a product by placing icons on a flowline; Flash and Director are timeline based, ToolBook is page based.

questions.q: Alpha-beta pruning is an optimisation technique used with which algorithm?
questions.exp: Alpha-beta pruning skips branches of the minimax game tree that cannot affect the final decision.

questions.q: Which transform is the basis of JPEG image compression?
options: Fourier transform on the whole image
questions.exp: Baseline JPEG applies the DCT to 8×8 blocks, then quantizes and entropy-codes the coefficients.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of reducing overfitting?
options: Adding many more layers and parameters without extra data
questions.exp: Increasing model capacity without more data usually worsens overfitting; the others are regularisation techniques.

questions.q: Image sharpening is generally achieved using a
questions.exp: High-pass (e.g. Laplacian) filters emphasise edges and fine detail.

questions.q: In MPEG video compression, an I-frame is
options: predicted from a future frame only
coded independently without reference to other frames
a frame that stores only motion vectors
a frame that is dropped during playback
questions.exp: I-frames (intra-coded) are self-contained and serve as reference points for P and B frames.

questions.q: Hill-climbing search can fail to find the global optimum mainly because it may get stuck at
options: a local maximum, plateau or ridge
a node with no successors only
questions.exp: Hill climbing moves only to better neighbours, so it halts at local maxima, plateaus or ridges.

questions.q: A decision tree algorithm such as ID3 chooses the attribute for splitting a node using
options: the lowest number of distinct values
questions.exp: ID3 selects the attribute giving the greatest reduction in entropy, i.e. highest information gain.

questions.q: The "naive" assumption of the Naive Bayes classifier is that
options: features are conditionally independent given the class
the data contains no missing values
questions.exp: Independence given the class lets the likelihood be written as the product of P(xi | class).

questions.q: Uniform-cost search always expands the node with the lowest
options: path cost g(n) from the start node
questions.exp: Uniform-cost search orders the frontier by cumulative path cost g(n) and is optimal.

questions.q: The main purpose of histogram equalization of an image is to
options: improve the contrast of the image
reduce the file size of the image
questions.exp: Equalization spreads the gray levels over the full range, enhancing global contrast.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an unsupervised learning algorithm?
questions.exp: K-means groups unlabeled data into clusters; the others need labeled training data.

questions.q: A semantic network is a knowledge representation scheme in which knowledge is represented as
options: a collection of slots and fillers inside frames
a table of rows and columns
a graph of nodes (concepts) connected by labelled arcs (relations)
questions.exp: Semantic networks use nodes for objects/concepts and labelled edges for relationships such as is-a.

questions.q: Backpropagation in a multilayer neural network is used to
options: compute the error gradient and update weights using gradient descent
increase the number of hidden layers
questions.exp: Backpropagation propagates the output error backwards to compute gradients for weight updates.

questions.q: A classifier produces TP = 40, FP = 10, FN = 20 and TN = 30. What is its precision?
questions.exp: Precision = TP/(TP+FP) = 40/50 = 0.80.

questions.q: Which first-order logic statement represents "Some students are clever"?
questions.exp: The existential quantifier goes with a conjunction; ∀ goes with implication.

questions.q: A CD-quality audio stream uses 44.1 kHz sampling, 16 bits per sample and 2 channels. Its uncompressed data rate in bits per second is
A binary classifier gives TP = 50, TN = 30, FP = 10 and FN = 10. Its accuracy is
questions.exp: Accuracy = (TP+TN)/total = 80/100 = 80%.

questions.q: A video of 10 seconds is played at 25 frames per second and each uncompressed frame needs 1 MB. The total uncompressed size is
In STRIPS-style planning, an action is described by its
options: heuristic value and path cost only
preconditions, add list and delete list
questions.exp: STRIPS actions list preconditions that must hold, facts added and facts deleted by the action.

questions.q: A model that gives very high accuracy on training data but much lower accuracy on unseen test data is said to be
questions.exp: Overfitting means the model memorises training data, including noise, and fails to generalise.

questions.q: A tree has root S with children A and B (in that order); A has children C and D; B has child E. The depth-first (left-first) visiting order is
options: S, A, B, C, D, E
S, A, C, D, B, E
S, B, E, A, D, C
S, A, C, B, D, E
questions.exp: DFS goes as deep as possible first: S, A, C, back to D, then B, E. The BFS order would be S, A, B, C, D, E.

questions.q: Frame-based knowledge representation was introduced by
questions.exp: Marvin Minsky proposed frames in 1975 as structures of slots and fillers for stereotyped situations.

questions.q: The 'Chinese Room' argument, which is directed against the claim that a program can truly understand, was proposed by
questions.exp: John Searle's 1980 thought experiment argues that symbol manipulation alone does not give understanding.

questions.q: Which first-order logic statement represents 'All humans are mortal'?
questions.exp: A universal statement about a category is expressed with ∀ and an implication.

questions.q: In multimedia project design, a storyboard is
options: a database of all copyrighted assets
a sequence of sketches showing screens, media elements and navigation
questions.exp: The storyboard is a design-phase document planning each screen and its interactions before authoring.

questions.q: In a grid, the Manhattan distance heuristic from (1, 1) to the goal (4, 5) is
In reinforcement learning, an agent learns by
options: reducing the number of input features
interacting with an environment and receiving rewards or penalties
questions.exp: RL agents learn a policy that maximises cumulative reward through trial and error.

questions.q: Part-of-speech (POS) tagging in NLP is the process of
options: assigning grammatical categories such as noun or verb to each word
questions.exp: POS tagging labels each token with its grammatical class.

questions.q: In frame-based knowledge representation, a slot value that is not defined in a child frame is normally obtained from
options: its parent frame through is-a inheritance (or a default value)
the inference engine's working memory only
questions.exp: Frames form an is-a hierarchy; children inherit slot values and defaults from parents unless overridden.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes forward chaining from backward chaining?
options: Forward chaining is goal-driven and backward chaining is data-driven
Forward chaining is data-driven and backward chaining is goal-driven
questions.exp: Forward chaining starts from known facts and derives new ones; backward chaining starts from a goal and looks for supporting facts.

questions.q: A heuristic function h(n) is called admissible if it
options: never overestimates the actual cost to reach the goal
always overestimates the cost to reach the goal
questions.exp: Admissibility means h(n) ≤ true cost from n to goal, which makes A* optimal.

questions.q: In natural language processing, stemming refers to
options: finding the meaning of a sentence
reducing a word to its root form
questions.exp: Stemming strips affixes, e.g. 'playing' and 'played' become 'play'.

questions.q: In propositional logic, the implication P → Q is logically equivalent to
questions.exp: P → Q is false only when P is true and Q is false, which matches ¬P ∨ Q.
